This is a Java course project for students. When you write documentation:

- Write Javadoc for every public class, constructor, method and protected field.
- Use @param, @return and @throws (one @throws for each exception the method can throw).
- Say what happens with bad input: does the method throw an exception, or return false or -1?
- For recursive methods, name the base case.
- For algorithms, give the time complexity in Big-O.
- For equals methods, say exactly which fields the method compares.
- Never describe behavior that is not in the code. If you are unsure, write TODO(verify).
- Do not change any code. Only add or edit comments.

Write in the style of ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English:

- Keep each sentence to 20 words or fewer. Write one idea in each sentence.
- Use the active voice and the present tense: "Returns the index", not "The index is returned".
- Use simple words with one meaning: "use", not "utilize"; "make sure", not "ensure"; "can", not "may".
- Use the same word for the same thing every time.
- Do not use an -ing word when a normal verb is possible.
